info.desc: Korn (printed and stylized as KoЯn) is the debut studio album by the American nu metal band Korn. It was released on October 11, 1994, through Immortal and Epic Records. Before recording the album, the band was approached by Immortal/Epic Records after a performance in Huntington Beach, California. The band signed to their label because they did not want to "sign away all of their creative freedom". The band would record at Indigo Ranch Studios in Malibu, California, with producer Ross Robinson, who also produced their 1993 demo Neidermayer's Mind. The recording took place from May to June 1994. podcast.body: Korn's self-titled debut album, released in 1994, features unsettling artwork depicting an eight-year-old girl, Justine Ferrarra, on a swing in a playground. A menacing shadow with lobster-like claws, cast by co-art director Dante Ariola, looms over her. The back cover maintains the sinister theme by showing the same playground but with the girl conspicuously missing. "It features a little girl dressed in a school uniform on a swing in a playground with an unseen figure casting a menacing shadow with lobster-like claws."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Stories Behind Iconic Album Covers Part 2
